name: The direct object
definition: The manṣūb noun on which the act falls, such as ʿamran in ḍaraba zaydun ʿamran.
body: In ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا (Zayd struck ʿAmr), ʿamran is the mafʿūl bihi: the striking fell on him. Only a transitive verb (mutaʿaddī) takes one; قَامَ (he stood) takes none.
Al-Ājurrūmiyya defines it as the manṣūb noun on which the act falls. It can also be a pronoun: نَصَرَنِي (he helped me), where the -nī is the object.

examples.text: Zayd struck ʿAmr: ʿamran is the object.
The student wrote the lesson: al-darsa is the object.
